assertions: Lilly will purchase Master B.'s houses — the bargain will be perfected and the houses in the Strand will become his, not break off
The seller is treatable and willing to deal: negotiation will reach agreement rather than ending in refusal or a third party taking the houses
The price will abate below the seller's first demand of £530 — Lilly will not have to pay the full first asking price
His money is not presently in hand and will be delayed at first, signified by Mercury lord of the 2nd retrograde, matching that his own money cannot be called in for six months
Despite that delay he will procure money in time to pay for the purchase and complete payment within the term allowed, so lack of ready money will not defeat the purchase

The transaction will be slow and drawn out by retrograde significators (Mercury and Saturn) and a square translation, but the square out of signs of long ascension works more like a trine and will not prevent perfection
The houses themselves are essentially sound with no material hidden defect — Saturn lord of the 4th has no material debility except retrogradation and cadency — and the possession will be lasting
method: Horary astrology (Lilly, Christian Astrology Book II) — whole-sign/classical horary significators: 1st querent, 7th seller, 4th houses, 2nd money, 11th hopes; reception, application, translation of light
reasoning: Lord of 7th is also lord of 11th, Lilly's hopes, showing seller and hope coincide. Venus (seller's significator) near 7th cusp and in exaltation receiving the Sun in the 7th, and Venus applying by trine to Saturn lord of the 4th (the houses), perfects seller-to-house agreement. Moon translating light by square out of signs of long ascension mitigates the square to a trine-like perfection. Saturn lord of 4th otherwise undebilitated supports sound, durable property. Sole impediment is Mercury lord of 2nd retrograde: money delayed/not callable for six months, causing slowness only, not denial — retrograde also signifies money returning/called back in time.
summary: Yes — Lilly should and will buy the houses, at less than £530, and will get the money in time to pay despite initial delay.
